kp.k: Practitioner reports increasing reliance on general-purpose Claude
kp.d: In his 27 February 2026 post, Shapiro says Claude increasingly constitutes essentially his entire legal-practice AI toolkit, explicitly distinguishing his choice from Harvey, CoCounsel and Spellbook. This is a first-person account of tool adoption, not a comparative performance study or evidence of profession-wide adoption.
qs: The answer, increasingly, is @claudeai. That's basically it.
Not Harvey. Not CoCounsel. Not Spellbook. A general-purpose AI that I've taught how I practice law.

kp.k: Personalised general-purpose AI is the stated practice approach
kp.d: Shapiro describes teaching a general-purpose AI how he practices law. The supplied document does not explain the adaptation method or specific workflows: it contains only the thread's opening post, while the remainder and the linked same-day article are not included.
qs: A general-purpose AI that I've taught how I practice law.
Neither the rest of the thread nor the article is held here; the article is a separate record.

kp.k: Lawyer inquiries indicate interest in his AI toolkit
kp.d: Shapiro reports receiving numerous inquiries from lawyers about his practice's AI technology over the preceding couple of weeks. The account supplies no count or sample characteristics and reports inquiries rather than those lawyers' own adoption decisions.
qs: Over the past couple weeks I've had a ton of lawyers reach out to ask me what AI tech I'm using in my legal practice.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Shapiro reports increasingly using general-purpose Claude, taught how he practises law, rather than named specialist legal-AI products.
pts.d: This is a claim about Shapiro's own practice and choice of technology, not an explicit prediction that general-purpose AI will replace specialist legal-AI vendors across the market. He identifies Claude as effectively his AI stack and distinguishes it from Harvey, CoCounsel and Spellbook. The supplied post does not specify tasks, workflow changes, performance improvements or effects on legal fees or staffing.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The evidence offered is a first-person account of practice use and anecdotal reports of interest from other lawyers.
pts.d: Shapiro reports his own technology use and says many lawyers have recently asked him about it. No comparative testing, measured outcomes, client cases or implementation details appear in the supplied post. Although it introduces an explanation with 'Here's how I use it:', the rest of the thread and the linked article are not supplied and cannot establish additional claims here. Post engagement figures document reach, not legal-AI effectiveness or adoption.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The claim concerns current and increasing reliance on Claude as of 27 February 2026, with no future deadline or forecast.
pts.d: The reported inquiries occurred over the preceding couple of weeks. 'Increasingly' indicates an ongoing shift in Shapiro's own use, while 'basically' qualifies the apparent exclusivity of Claude. His description concerns a general-purpose system he says he has taught how he practises law; the supplied text does not explain that process or establish results for an unconfigured system.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The directly described user is Shapiro; other lawyers appear as interested peers, and specialist legal-AI vendors appear as alternatives he does not use.
pts.d: The supplied profile identifies Shapiro as a managing partner and corporate lawyer, locating this account in practising corporate law. Other lawyers are described as seeking information, not as adopting Claude themselves. Harvey, CoCounsel and Spellbook are named as excluded choices in his account, but no market-wide loss of demand is claimed. Effects on clients, the public, access to justice or employment are not stated.
